topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Cones: Dandelin Spheres
target_audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: The Slicing Problem
lecture_lines: Cones are surfaces formed by rotation.
animations: Create 3D cone #FFFFFF. Rotate it around vertical axis.
Animate a plane #FFFF00 slicing the cone.
Isolate the resulting conic section curve #FF00FF.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Imagine two spheres inside a cone.
Spheres touch the cone in circles.
Points of contact are called foci.
This reveals the geometry behind conics.
animations: Draw cone and two spheres #00FFFF inside tangent to it.
Highlight circular contact points between spheres and cone #00FF00.
Place a plane #FF0000 intersecting the cone and both spheres.
Mark intersection points on the plane #FFFF00 as focal points.
Fade all elements slowly to establish the geometric setup #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Ellipse Connection
lecture_lines: Consider a point on the ellipse.
This sum equals the path distance.
animations: Display ellipse slice curve #FF00FF on the plane.
Plot two Dandelin focal points #FFFF00 on the plane.
Draw lines from a point on the curve to the foci #FF9900.
Animate the point moving along the ellipse curve.
Show that the sum of distances to the foci stays constant #FF9900.

sections.title: Universal Application
animations: Transition setup from ellipse to parabola using one sphere #00FFFF.
Transition setup from parabola to hyperbola using two spheres #00FFFF.
Overlay all conic section intersection curves in different colors #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
animations: Assemble all slices: circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola #FFFFFF.
Highlight the Dandelin sphere in each of these configurations #FFFF00.
Fade everything to white text summary: 'Dandelin Spheres Unify' #FFFFFF.
